before.reason: For the tested original study (Azzi and Ehrenberg, 1975), the direct replication of the church-attendance equations in Section I explicitly yields 'mixed support': female mean attendance exceeds male mean attendance in 8 of 9 denominations, the predicted age-attendance profile holds in 16 of 18 cases, and control variables perform similarly to the previous paper, but in contrast the female age-attendance profile is steeper than the male profile in only 4 of 9 cases, education increases attendance, and family income has no systematic effect. Section II (1969 National Jewish Population Study) supports the life-cycle and relative-wage implications while noting lower mean female than male synagogue attendance as a 'contradiction' in footnote 9, and the conclusion notes that 'the evidence is not totally unambiguous' while supporting the usefulness of the general household time-allocation framework. Both shipped and blind coded 'mixed', with blind properly evaluating the outcome against Azzi and Ehrenberg (1975).

before.quote: Fourth, in order to replicate Nicolaou et al. (2018), we define the dependent variable, the control variables, and the sample as closely to this study as possible. Our failure to find significant effects does not rule out that 2D:4D is associated with other outcomes related to entrepreneurship such as entrepreneurial intent, as reported by Bönte et al. (2016) for university students; however, it is unclear in how far entrepreneurial intent among students will materialize in actual entrepreneurial behavior later in life. It is also possible that biological factors, including 2D:4D, affect younger persons more than older persons, who have been subject to more intervening nonbiological influences (Bönte et al., 2017). In an additional not preregistered exploratory analysis, we test for an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in our data using a measure of entrepreneurial intent similar to one of the measures used by Bönte et al. (2016). We find no statistically significant or suggestive evidence of an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in this analysis.
before.reason: Evaluating the outcome for the resolved tested original Bönte et al. (2016) (whereas the shipped row's quote concerned self-employment for the misidentified original): the Introduction and Results note that Bönte et al. (2016) reported significant negative associations between right-hand 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent among university students and argued the effect is stronger in younger individuals, whereas this paper's corresponding SOEP-IS regressions find no statistically significant or suggestive association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent and no interaction with age.
